lines.text: A bad jobs report helped push stocks to a record.
lines.say: A bad jobs report helped push stocks to a record.

lines.text: That was August 7, 2026, the day the July report showed 23,000 jobs lost.
lines.say: That was August seventh, twenty twenty-six, the day the July report showed twenty-three thousand jobs lost.

scene.headline: US lost 23,000 jobs in July; S&P 500 closes at record

lines.text: The jobs report comes from the Bureau of Labor Statistics, usually on the first Friday of the month.
lines.say: The jobs report comes from the Bureau of Labor Statistics, usually on the first Friday of the month.

lines.text: For July 2026, economists expected 83,000 jobs. The first count showed a loss of 23,000.
lines.say: For July, economists expected eighty-three thousand jobs. The first count showed a loss of twenty-three thousand.

lines.text: Fewer jobs meant less pressure on the Fed to raise rates. Yields fell, stocks rose.
lines.say: Fewer jobs meant less pressure on the Fed to raise rates. Yields fell, stocks rose.

lines.text: Then August 2026 flipped it: 162,000 jobs, versus about 55,000 expected.
lines.say: Then August flipped it: a hundred sixty-two thousand jobs, versus about fifty-five thousand expected.

lines.text: Rate hike bets jumped, and the S&P 500 fell 0.38% that day.
lines.say: Rate hike bets jumped, and the S and P five hundred fell zero point three eight percent that day.

lines.text: The twist: the first number isn't final. A month later, July's -23,000 was revised to +21,000.
lines.say: The twist: the first number isn't final. A month later, July's minus twenty-three thousand was revised to plus twenty-one thousand.

lines.text: So markets don't trade the jobs number. They trade the gap between expected and actual.
lines.say: So markets don't trade the jobs number. They trade the gap between expected and actual.

post.title: Why a bad jobs report sent stocks to a record
post.ig:
A bad jobs report helped push stocks to a record. Here's why.

July 2026: economists expected +83,000 jobs, the first count showed -23,000. Yields fell and the S&P 500 closed at a record on Aug 7, 2026.
August 2026: +162,000 jobs vs about 55,000 expected. Rate hike bets jumped and the S&P 500 fell 0.38% on Sept 4, 2026.
The first number isn't final: July's first revision took it to +21,000.

Sources: BLS Employment Situation, CNBC, Reuters, Yahoo Finance (Aug-Sept 2026).
News and education, not financial advice.
